1	import SwiftUI

3	/// Every number the VCS toolbar uses, in one place.
4	///
5	/// The horizontal ones are chosen so the toolbar aligns *by construction* with the section header
6	/// beneath it rather than by eye: `outerInset` + `glyphSlot` + `glyphSpacing` puts the branch glyph's
7	/// centre and the branch name's left edge exactly where `SectionHeader`'s chevron centre and title land
8	/// (`InspectorSplitView.headerLabel` uses the same 12 / 12 / 7).
9	enum VCSToolbarMetrics {
10	  /// 11pt semibold title (13pt line) + 1pt + 10pt caption (12pt line) = 26, plus 5pt above and below.
11	  /// Two lines genuinely don't fit the section headers' 34pt, and 36 also reads as a distinct band.
12	  ///
13	  /// The count pills sit on the title line, so that row is as tall as a `.caption2` capsule rather than
14	  /// 13pt whenever one is shown. That takes the stack a couple of points past 26 and leaves the band
15	  /// unchanged — the slack was already there, which is why the pills could move up without this number
16	  /// moving with them.
17	  static let height: CGFloat = 36
18	  static let outerInset: CGFloat = 12
19	  /// Inner edges of the segments — tighter than `outerInset` so the middle segment isn't starved.
20	  static let innerInset: CGFloat = 8
21	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron `.frame(width: 12)`.
22	  static let glyphSlot: CGFloat = 12
23	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s `HStack(spacing: 7)`.
24	  static let glyphSpacing: CGFloat = 7
25	  /// Between the inspector's 11pt header glyphs and the pane bar's 13pt action icons: it has to hold
26	  /// against a bold 11pt title without reading as a pane-bar button.
27	  static let glyph: CGFloat = 12
28	  /// 22pt well plus 4pt either side — `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.footprint` rounded to a divider-bounded cell.
29	  static let fetchWidth: CGFloat = 30
30	
31	  static let titleFont = Font.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)
32	  static let captionFont = Font.system(size: 10)
33	  /// The single-line states. A lone 10pt dim line in a 36pt bar reads as a rendering bug, so the solo
34	  /// subtitle is a step up in both size and contrast.
35	  static let soloFont = Font.system(size: 11)
36	
37	  /// ONE floor, shared by the branch and sync segments, because the two are equal width.
38	  ///
39	  /// Equal width is what makes the bar read as two halves plus a button rather than three arbitrary
40	  /// cells, and it's only achievable if both segments have the same floor as well as the same `maxWidth`:
41	  /// an `HStack` divides slack evenly, so unequal minimums stay unequal by their difference at every
42	  /// width. The value is set by the narrowest inspector — `2 × 114 + fetchWidth + 2 dividers = 260`,
43	  /// exactly the 260pt minimum. (It replaces a 100/126 split with a 220 cap on the branch cell; the cap
44	  /// existed to stop a short name hoarding width, which an even division already does.)
45	  static let segmentMinWidth: CGFloat = 114
46	
47	  /// Verbatim from `PRNumberBadge`, so the toolbar's pill matches the ref pill 40pt below it.
48	  static let pillHorizontalPadding: CGFloat = 5
49	  static let pillVerticalPadding: CGFloat = 1
50	  /// The pill's ↑/↓ glyph. Smaller than `glyph` on purpose — it sits inside a `.caption2` capsule and
51	  /// has to read as a direction marker beside the count, not as an icon in its own right.
52	  static let pillArrowGlyph: CGFloat = 7
53	}

55	/// The VCS toolbar: current branch, a sync segment that shows and performs the right remote action, and
56	/// a fetch button — divided into three full-height cells.
57	///
58	/// Lives at the top of `RightInspector`, above the section stack, and only for the Changes activity
59	/// section. Deliberately a plain SwiftUI view inside the inspector's content and **never** a `.toolbar`
60	/// modifier: the window toolbar is kept an empty AppKit `NSToolbar` because a SwiftUI toolbar item's
61	/// overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a multi-second app hang.
62	struct VCSToolbar: View {
63	  /// Observed EXPLICITLY, like `HistoryPanel`'s and `FilesPanel`'s models.
64	  ///
65	  /// `RemoteStateModel` is its own `ObservableObject`; `AppStore` merely holds it and does not forward
66	  /// its `objectWillChange`. Reading it through `store.remoteState` alone renders the first state and
67	  /// then never repaints — clicking Push set `inFlight`, ran the push and recorded the result, and the
68	  /// toolbar showed none of it. Caught by `VCSToolbarUITests.testClickingPushRequestsAPush`.
69	  @ObservedObject var model: RemoteStateModel
70	
71	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
72	  /// `ThemeService.shared` isn't observed by SwiftUI, so a theme switch would otherwise leave the
73	  /// hairlines stale. Same pattern as `ActivityBar`.
74	  @State private var themeTick = 0
75	
76	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
77	
78	  /// The toolbar's whole state, resolved in one place so the three segments can't disagree.
79	  private func presentation(now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
80	    VCSSyncPresenter.make(
81	      state: model.snapshot, hasTarget: model.target != nil,
82	      toolsUsable: store.vcsAllowsRemoteActions(vcs: model.target?.vcs ?? "git"),
83	      // `activeAction`, not `inFlight`: the label must describe THIS workroom. `inFlight` is the
84	      // model-wide lock, so rendering it directly showed "Pushing…" on a workroom that wasn't pushing.
85	      activity: model.activeAction.map { .running($0) } ?? .idle,
86	      failure: model.lastFailure, lastAction: model.lastAction, now: now)
87	  }
88	
89	  var body: some View {
90	    // Only the relative timestamp needs to tick, so `TimelineView` wraps the whole bar but the schedule
91	    // is coarse (30s) and every other value is already `@Published`. Confining it to just the timestamp
92	    // `Text` would need the presentation recomputed per-subview, which is worse.
93	    TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 30)) { context in
94	      let p = presentation(now: context.date)
95	      HStack(spacing: 0) {
96	        // The branch and sync cells are EQUAL width: same floor, same `maxWidth: .infinity`, and no
97	        // `layoutPriority` on either. All three parts are load-bearing — an `HStack` splits slack evenly
98	        // only between views that are equally flexible, so a priority override or a different floor
99	        // reintroduces the imbalance. (An earlier version gave sync `layoutPriority(1)` AND
100	        // `maxWidth: .infinity`, so it was offered the whole width first and claimed it, pinning the
101	        // branch cell at its floor even in a wide inspector: `feature/login` rendered as `fe…gin`.)
102	        VCSBranchSegment(name: branchName, vcs: model.target?.vcs)
103	          .frame(minWidth: VCSToolbarMetrics.segmentMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
104	        divider
105	        VCSSyncSegment(presentation: p, onAct: { perform(p.action) })
106	          .frame(minWidth: VCSToolbarMetrics.segmentMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
107	        divider
108	        VCSFetchSegment(
109	          isRunning: model.activeAction == .fetch,
110	          isEnabled: model.canFetch
111	            && store.vcsAllowsRemoteActions(vcs: model.target?.vcs ?? "git"),
112	          onFetch: { perform(.fetch) }
113	        )
114	        .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.fetchWidth)
115	      }
116	      .frame(height: VCSToolbarMetrics.height)
117	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
118	      .overlay(alignment: .bottom) { theme.border.frame(height: 1) }
119	      .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
120	      .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar")
121	    }
122	    .id(themeTick)
123	    .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .themeDidChange)) { _ in themeTick += 1 }
124	  }
125	
126	  /// Full-bleed, unlike `TitlebarDivider` (a 14pt inline group rule) — it's what makes the three cells
127	  /// read as segments rather than as a row of controls.
128	  private var divider: some View {
129	    Rectangle().fill(theme.border).frame(width: 1).frame(maxHeight: .infinity)
130	  }
131	
132	  /// Read through the one accessor every branch-showing surface uses, so this can't disagree with the
133	  /// status bar or the sidebar.
134	  private var branchName: String? {
135	    model.target.flatMap { store.branchName(for: $0.sid) }
136	  }
137	
138	  /// Hands straight to the store, which owns the dirty-tree confirmation gate.
139	  ///
140	  /// The gate used to live here, and that was the bug: the Source Control menu calls
141	  /// `performRemoteAction` directly, so ⌥⇧⌘P autostashed a dirty tree with no warning while this button
142	  /// warned. A gate only one of two entry points honours isn't a gate.
143	  private func perform(_ action: VCSRemoteAction?) {
144	    guard let action else { return }
145	    store.performRemoteAction(action)
146	  }
147	}

149	/// Segment 1: the current branch. **Display only — not a control.**
150	///
151	/// Not a dropdown, and not a button either. Workrooms **are** branches — a workroom's identity is its
152	/// directory name, with no branch field anywhere in the config — so switching a workroom's branch would
153	/// make its name permanently wrong, and the jj equivalent (`jj new <bookmark>`) was reproduced removing
154	/// a file from the working copy and orphaning the workroom's commit. With switching gone there is no
155	/// action left that belongs on the branch name, so this is a label: no `Button`, no hover well, no
156	/// chevron. Each of those would promise something that doesn't happen.
157	///
158	/// It still carries a `.help` — middle truncation hides the middle of a long name, and the tooltip is
159	/// how you read the whole thing — plus a right-click "Copy Branch Name". Neither is a click action.
160	private struct VCSBranchSegment: View {
161	  let name: String?
162	  /// The target's backend (`"git"` / `"jj"`), nil when nothing is selected. Every string in this segment
163	  /// derives from it through `VCSSyncPresenter`, so the caption, the tooltip and the spoken label can't
164	  /// drift out of agreement — and the mapping stays unit-testable rather than inline here.
165	  let vcs: String?
166	
167	  private var noun: String { VCSSyncPresenter.refNoun(vcs: vcs) }
168	  private var caption: String { VCSSyncPresenter.refCaption(vcs: vcs) }
169	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
170	
171	  var body: some View {
172	    HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
173	      Image(systemName: "arrow.triangle.branch")
174	        .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
175	        .foregroundStyle(theme.fgMuted)
176	        .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
177	      // The caption is unconditional. It used to sit in a `ViewThatFits` ladder against a name-only
178	      // variant, which dropped it far more often than intended and in the wrong circumstances:
179	      // `ViewThatFits` measures each variant's IDEAL width, and a `.lineLimit(1)` truncating `Text`
180	      // reports its FULL untruncated string as its ideal — so the caption was vetoed by a long *name*,
181	      // never by a narrow cell. jj repos lost it almost always (bookmark names, or the ancestor bookmark
182	      // a workspace's unbookmarked `@` resolves to, run longer than a `feature/login`) while git repos
183	      // kept it, which is exactly the asymmetry that got reported. The name truncates instead; at the
184	      // 114pt floor the caption truncates too, which is honest degradation rather than a silent drop.
185	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {
186	        Text(caption)
187	          .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.captionFont)
188	          .foregroundStyle(theme.fgDim)
189	          .lineLimit(1)
190	          .truncationMode(.tail)
191	        nameText
192	      }
193	      Spacer(minLength: 0)
194	    }
195	    .padding(.leading, VCSToolbarMetrics.outerInset)
196	    .padding(.trailing, VCSToolbarMetrics.innerInset)
197	    // The cell's own layout, WITHOUT `vcsToolbarSegment`'s hover fill: that treatment marks a segment as
198	    // clickable, and this one isn't. `contentShape` is still needed so the tooltip and context menu have
199	    // the full cell as their hit region rather than just the glyph and text glyphs.
200	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
201	    .contentShape(Rectangle())
202	    .help(name ?? "No \(noun) resolved yet")
203	    // A `Button` was implicitly ONE accessibility element; a plain `HStack` is not, so without this its
204	    // caption and name would be exposed as two unrelated strings.
205	    .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
206	    // Caption AND name in the LABEL, not split across label + value.
207	    //
208	    // `.accessibilityValue` does not survive on this element: once it stopped being a `Button` and got
209	    // collapsed with `children: .ignore`, AppKit maps it to a static-text element whose value the
210	    // modifier no longer sets — it read back as the empty string, which failed both tests that assert the
211	    // name. (`ChangesPanel`'s combined header shows the mirror-image of the same mapping: there the
212	    // children's text lands in the VALUE and the label comes back empty.) The label is the one field that
213	    // reliably carries what we set, so both parts go in it — and VoiceOver reads it as one phrase, which
214	    // is what a two-line label is anyway.
215	    .accessibilityLabel("\(caption): \(name ?? "unknown")")
216	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.branch")
217	    .contextMenu {
218	      // Offered as a menu item rather than making the label selectable: `.textSelection(.enabled)`
219	      // swallows real mouseDown, which would stop this segment being clickable with an actual mouse
220	      // while synthetic test clicks kept passing.
221	      if let name {
222	        Button("Copy \(noun.capitalized) Name") {
223	          NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
224	          NSPasteboard.general.setString(name, forType: .string)
225	        }
226	      }
227	    }
228	  }
229	
230	  /// `.middle` truncation, because a long branch's distinguishing part is usually its tail
231	  /// (`joel/history-refs-pill`) — the same reasoning the Changes header and status bar already follow.
232	  private var nameText: some View {
233	    Text(name ?? "—")
234	      .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.titleFont)
235	      .lineLimit(1)
236	      .truncationMode(.middle)
237	  }
238	}
239	
240	/// Segment 2: what to do about the remote, and doing it.
241	///
242	/// Line order is inverted relative to segment 1 — bold title over dim subtitle — which is what the
243	/// reference design specifies. The consequence is that the two segments' bold lines do **not** share a
244	/// baseline: both blocks are 26pt and vertically centred, so a caption-first block sits low and a
245	/// title-first block sits high. The full-height divider between them is what makes that read as two
246	/// groups rather than a misalignment. Called out because it looks like a bug and isn't.
247	private struct VCSSyncSegment: View {
248	  let presentation: VCSSyncPresentation
249	  let onAct: () -> Void
250	
251	  @State private var hovering = false
252	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
253	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
254	
255	  private var toneColor: Color {
256	    switch presentation.tone {
257	    case .normal: return theme.fgDim
258	    case .warning: return theme.warning
259	    case .failure: return theme.failure
260	    }
261	  }
262	
263	  var body: some View {
264	    Button(action: onAct) {
265	      HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
266	        if let symbol = presentation.symbol {
267	          Image(systemName: symbol)
268	            .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
269	            .foregroundStyle(presentation.tone == .normal ? theme.fgMuted : toneColor)
270	            .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
271	        } else if presentation.action != nil, isRunning {
272	          ProgressView().controlSize(.mini).frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
273	        }
274	        content
275	      }
276	      .padding(.horizontal, VCSToolbarMetrics.innerInset)
277	      .vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: hovering && presentation.isEnabled, reduceMotion: reduceMotion)
278	    }
279	    .buttonStyle(.plain)
280	    .disabled(!presentation.isEnabled)
281	    // Deliberately NO disabled dim, unlike `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`. Every disabled state here is a
282	    // MESSAGE, not a withheld action — "No remote configured", "No repository", "Pushing…", and the
283	    // `.failure`-toned retry line — so all of them have to stay readable; the suppressed hover well is
284	    // what says "not clickable". An `.opacity(0.4)` here also COMPOUNDS: the text is already
285	    // `fgMuted` (fg @ 0.65), so it landed at an effective 0.26, fainter than `fgDim` (0.40) — the
286	    // placeholder tier — and dimmed error copy along with it. That convention's 0.4 is right only
287	    // because it sits on full-strength `fg`.
288	    .onHover { hovering = $0 }
289	    .help(presentation.help)
290	    .accessibilityLabel(presentation.accessibility)
291	    .accessibilityValue(presentation.accessibilityValue)
292	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.sync")
293	    // Only when a lock file is blocking the repo. Workroom deliberately doesn't delete it — telling a
294	    // live git's lock from an abandoned one isn't possible from outside the process, and deleting a live
295	    // one corrupts the index — so the fix is the user's to make, and these hand them the file rather
296	    // than making them retype a path out of a tooltip.
297	    .contextMenu {
298	      if let lockPath = presentation.lockPath {
299	        Button("Copy Lock File Path") {
300	          NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
301	          NSPasteboard.general.setString(lockPath, forType: .string)
302	        }
303	        Button("Reveal Lock File in Finder") {
304	          NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([URL(fileURLWithPath: lockPath)])
305	        }
306	      }
307	    }
308	  }
309	
310	  private var isRunning: Bool { presentation.title?.hasSuffix("…") == true }
311	
312	  @ViewBuilder private var content: some View {
313	    if presentation.isSingleLine {
314	      HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
315	        // Centred and a step up in size/contrast: a lone dim 10pt line in a 36pt bar reads as broken.
316	        Text(presentation.subtitle)
317	          .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.soloFont)
318	          .foregroundStyle(presentation.tone == .normal ? theme.fgMuted : toneColor)
319	          .lineLimit(1)
320	          .truncationMode(.tail)
321	        Spacer(minLength: 4)
322	        pills
323	      }
324	    } else {
325	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {
326	        // The pills ride the TITLE line rather than the whole cell. As siblings of this VStack they
327	        // narrowed BOTH lines, and the line they cost the most was the one that could least afford it:
328	        // the timestamp is the longest string in the bar ("Fetched 22 minutes ago") and the only one
329	        // whose full form is worth reading, while the title above it is short and has an abbreviation
330	        // ladder to fall back on. Now the timestamp gets the segment's whole width and the pills
331	        // compete only with the title, which is what the ladder is for.
332	        HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
333	          // Longest variant first — `ViewThatFits` takes the first that fits, so inverting this order
334	          // silently defeats the whole ladder. `VCSSyncPresentationTests` pins the ordering.
335	          ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
336	            ForEach(presentation.titleVariants, id: \.self) { variant in
337	              Text(variant).font(VCSToolbarMetrics.titleFont).lineLimit(1)
338	            }
339	          }
340	          Spacer(minLength: 4)
341	          pills
342	        }
343	        // The staleness caveat abbreviates but survives. It must NOT be the first thing dropped: the
344	        // count pill it qualifies is pinned, so losing the caveat first would leave an unverified number
345	        // standing alone.
346	        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
347	          Text(presentation.subtitle)
348	          Text(presentation.subtitleShort)
349	        }
350	        .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.captionFont)
351	        .foregroundStyle(toneColor)
352	        .lineLimit(1)
353	        .truncationMode(.tail)
354	      }
355	      // The cell no longer has a `Spacer` of its own to fill it, so the VStack claims the width — which
356	      // is also what lets the subtitle's ladder measure against the full cell.
357	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
358	    }
359	  }
360	
361	  /// Ahead first, then behind — the diverged order the presenter fixes (`↓` before `↑` is decided there,
362	  /// not here; this just renders `badge` then `secondaryBadge`).
363	  @ViewBuilder private var pills: some View {
364	    if let badge = presentation.badge { VCSCountPill(badge: badge) }
365	    if let secondary = presentation.secondaryBadge { VCSCountPill(badge: secondary) }
366	  }
367	}
368	
369	/// Segment 3: fetch.
370	///
371	/// `arrow.down.circle`, not `arrow.clockwise`: the Changes header's Refresh button is already
372	/// `arrow.clockwise` roughly 40pt below and 10pt to the left, and two near-identical circular-arrow
373	/// glyphs meaning different things (re-read local status vs contact the remote) is a real confusion.
374	/// The down-arrow also matches the ↓ direction language of the count pills.
375	private struct VCSFetchSegment: View {
376	  let isRunning: Bool
377	  let isEnabled: Bool
378	  let onFetch: () -> Void
379	
380	  @State private var hovering = false
381	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
382	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
383	
384	  var body: some View {
385	    Button(action: onFetch) {
386	      Group {
387	        if isRunning {
388	          // `.mini`, not `.small`: small is ~16pt and would overflow the 12pt glyph slot.
389	          ProgressView().controlSize(.mini)
390	        } else {
391	          Image(systemName: "arrow.down.circle")
392	            .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
393	            // Unlike segment 2 this IS a bare affordance, so unavailable should read as unavailable —
394	            // but as ONE tier, not a multiply. `fgDim` is fg @ 0.40, the same effective alpha
395	            // `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`'s `.opacity(0.4)` produces on its full-strength glyphs.
396	            .foregroundStyle(isEnabled ? theme.fgMuted : theme.fgDim)
397	        }
398	      }
399	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
400	      .vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: hovering && isEnabled, reduceMotion: reduceMotion)
401	    }
402	    .buttonStyle(.plain)
403	    .disabled(!isEnabled || isRunning)
404	    .onHover { hovering = $0 }
405	    .help(isRunning ? "Fetching…" : "Fetch from the remote")
406	    .accessibilityLabel("Fetch")
407	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.fetch")
408	  }
409	}
410	
411	/// A count pill: `5 ↑` / `3 ↓`.
412	///
413	/// Geometry and font copied from `PRNumberBadge` so it matches the ref pill in the Changes header just
414	/// below. Both directions use the same `surface` fill rather than hue-coding: the arrow carries the
415	/// direction (shape, not colour) and a count is a quantity, not a severity.
416	private struct VCSCountPill: View {
417	  let badge: VCSSyncPresentation.Badge
418	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
419	
420	  var body: some View {
421	    HStack(spacing: 2) {
422	      Text("\(badge.count)").font(.caption2).fontWeight(.semibold).monospacedDigit()
423	      Image(systemName: badge.direction == .ahead ? "arrow.up" : "arrow.down")
424	        .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.pillArrowGlyph, weight: .semibold))
425	    }
426	    .foregroundStyle(theme.fgMuted)
427	    .padding(.horizontal, VCSToolbarMetrics.pillHorizontalPadding)
428	    .padding(.vertical, VCSToolbarMetrics.pillVerticalPadding)
429	    .background(Capsule().fill(theme.surface))
430	    // The highest-information 30pt in the bar — it must never yield.
431	    .fixedSize()
432	    // The spoken form comes from the sync button's `accessibilityValue`; a pill read separately would
433	    // just be a bare number with no subject.
434	    .accessibilityHidden(true)
435	  }
436	}
437	
438	extension View {
439	  /// One hover treatment for all three segments: the whole divider-bounded cell fills.
440	  ///
441	  /// Deliberately not the 22pt inset well `InspectorHeaderButton` uses — that's right for a control
442	  /// floating in a header row, but inside a cell whose bounds are drawn by hairlines a small inner well
443	  /// reads as a mistake. Opacity is animated, never the view tree: an implicit tree animation
444	  /// interpolates a glyph's 1pt pixel re-round into a visible slide (see `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`).
445	  fileprivate func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: Bool, reduceMotion: Bool) -> some View {
446	    self
447	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
448	      .background(
449	        ThemeService.shared.tokens.hover
450	          .opacity(hovering ? 1 : 0)
451	          .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: 0.12), value: hovering)
452	      )
453	      .contentShape(Rectangle())
454	  }
455	}

content.text:
I've read the full file. The change is a pure SwiftUI layout reorganization inside `VCSToolbar.swift`:

- Moves the `VCSCountPill` rendering out of the outer `HStack` and into `content`, so pills now ride the title line instead of the whole cell.
- Wraps single-line and title branches in an `HStack` containing the pills.
- Adds `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` to the VStack so it claims the width previously held by the removed sibling Spacer.
- Extracts pill rendering into a `pills` private computed view.
- Adds a documentation comment about pill height.

There are no changes to:
- Any sink (no shell/exec, SQL, filesystem writes, network, deserialization, template/HTML rendering, logging/telemetry, IPC, auth/permission checks, or subprocess spawns).
- Any parser/validator, allowlist, or gate.
